steps.body: Two written numerals compare the same way: the one LATER in the counting song is GREATER. 8 beats 6 because counting reaches 6 first.
steps.narration: Two written numerals compare the same way: the one LATER in the counting song is GREATER. 8 beats 6 because counting reaches 6 first.

widget.prompt: What number comes right after 7? Hop one and tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 7 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 8.
9 goes one complete hop too far. One hop from 7 lands on 8.

widget.missFeedback: Count 1 on from 7: you land on 8.
widget.successFeedback: 8 — one hop forward, and one hop later in the song always means greater.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — a single hop forward reaches 8.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — right after 7 means one hop, stopping on 8.

options.label: 8 — it comes later in the song

predict.reveal: Position in the counting song is the whole meaning of greater; shape plays no part.

cml.actionGoal: Pair the groups one to one, or place both numbers in the counting song, for kcm greater numeral.
invariants: Comparison rests on two facts that never move: pairing one to one leaves the bigger group with leftovers, and a number later in the counting song always names more — which is what kcm greater numeral uses.
misconceptions: Judging by how much space a group fills, by the size of the things in it, or by which number was written first.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more joined the smaller group, would the pairing come out even?
